newsitem.title: TURKEY: Political caution drives Istanbul shares lower.
newsitem.headline: Political caution drives Istanbul shares lower.

text.p: Istanbul shares extended their earlier losses in late sales on Tuesday amid bearish sentiment due to mounting political uncertainty, brokers said.

They said the decline was mainly due to the awaited resignation of Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan for Wednesday to form a caretaker government to be headed by his conservative ally Tansu Ciller to prepare for snap polls.
The IMKB National-100 closed at 1,551, down 31 points, or 1.96 percent from Monday after brushing a low of 1,547 in the afternoon.
Trade volume was little changed at 12.92 trillion lira ($88.7 million), versus Monday's 12.10 trillion ($83.2 million).

"Technically, the market is losing strength because noone can forecast what will happen in the political arena amid such a chaos. Support is seen at the index's 1,550, 1,530 and 1,480 levels and resistance at 1,620 and 1,680," said Murat Ozkan of Emper securities.

"The market does not want the Islamist-conservative coalition to last. Selling emerges when the possibility rises that the ruling coalition will survive and buying picks up when this possibility fades," he added.

Members of the junior coalition partner True Path Party and the Turkish press say Erbakan will resign on Wednesday in a plan to swap jobs with Deputy Prime Minister Ciller to seek early polls by the end of 1997.
An eight-member far-right party leader with a key position in parliament said he would back government efforts to push the power transfer and election laws through parliament.
But Erbakan made no specific mention of the turnover plan in an hour-long speech to MPs of his Islam-based Welfare Party.

Brokers said the market was also discouraged by sharply higher overnight money and repo rates prompted by the central bank's action to further tighten liquidity to suppress fresh dollar demand which flared amid political uncertainty.

The Turkish Treasury sold only 3.05 trillion lira of two-year, inflation-indexed, three-month coupon payment bonds due to low demand caused by political worries. It had sold 198.1 trillion lira of similar bonds in the previous June 3 auction at the same risk premium, 32 percent.
Brokers said the weak sale in the auction further depressed buyers in the afternoon.
